title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
author: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
edition: 1818 first edition (three volumes); public domain. Chapter refs are 1818 numbering (the 1831 text shifts chapters).

entries.name: the creature

canon.quote: His yellow skin scarcely covered the work of muscles and arteries beneath
his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing; his teeth of a pearly whiteness
his watery eyes, that seemed almost of the same colour as the dun white sockets in which they were set
his shrivelled complexion, and straight black lips
of a gigantic stature; that is to say, about eight feet in height, and proportionably large

ruling.text: clothing: a plain dark cloak and rough worn clothes taken in the woods
ruling.why: book silent on dress at creation; he later finds and wears clothes

ruling.text: no neck bolts, no stitches across the forehead
ruling.why: book silent on the method of assembly; bolts and stitches come from the 1931 film

entries.prefer: book over the 1931 film look (green skin, flat-topped head, neck bolts)

misses.miss: draws the film look: green skin, flat head, bolts
misses.fix: describe yellow skin, long flowing black hair, black lips; keep 'Frankenstein' out of the prompt

checks.claim: skin reads yellowish, thin over muscle, not green or grey
long, lustrous, flowing black hair; no flat-topped head
eyes watery and nearly as pale as their sockets
no neck bolts or forehead stitches

canon.quote: a solitary chamber, or rather cell, at the top of the house
by the glimmer of the half-extinguished light

ruling.text: a small attic cell lit by one guttering candle; no lightning towers or electrical machinery
ruling.why: book names no apparatus; the machinery is from the films

misses.miss: a large stone laboratory with sparking coils
misses.fix: say 'small attic room, sloping ceiling, one candle', drop 'laboratory'

checks.claim: a small room at the top of a house, not a hall
lit by a single dim light, no electrical sparks
